summary: Extend the established Clinical Glass / Continuity Aurora system into a route-based, API-backed treatment-continuity experience: a patient-record-free public and pricing surface, a truthful local access gateway, calm role-minimized patient and caregiver views, dense staff and CareLink operations, and inspectable graph, timeline, provider, metrics, FHIR, and supportive-outreach evidence. The design keeps every pending, failure, conflict, outcome-unknown, recovery, and acknowledgment boundary visibly distinct so an external request, assignment, replay, or model result can never look like confirmed care continuity.
existing_design_system: docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md plus the implemented Clinical Glass / Continuity Aurora runtime tokens and components in frontend/src/index.css and frontend/src/components

visual_direction.layout: Preserve the public page's editorial hero, role storytelling, Continuity Field, operating-model story, Louisiana access context, FAQ, and official identity, but remove every Maria record, MRN, regimen, facility record, readiness graph, case row, and workspace preview from the public DOM and accessibility tree. Replace the public product-record proof with a record-free capability sequence built from generic owned-work labels, then add a pricing section sourced from one frontend configuration: Small Infusion Center Pilot at $18,000/year and $1,500/month billed annually, usage charges called out as separate, and a Custom pricing card for larger programs with Request a pilot / Talk to us actions only. The /access route is a centered four-entry workspace gateway with no scenario details: Google-style entry maps locally to Patient, Microsoft to Caregiver, Apple to Staff, and email to Transportation; each entry states the destination before activation and a compact boundary note says this controlled workspace selector does not verify identity. /patient and /caregiver retain an editorial single-action column. /staff uses the existing compact rail and a command canvas organized as current readiness, owned work, communications, transport, and evidence. /transport becomes a dedicated CareLink fulfillment workspace with a cutoff/eligibility header, outbound and return plan pair, mobility/accommodation facts, a stepwise lifecycle, and one contextual next action; the planned Uber Health and Lyft Concierge adapters appear only in a separate disabled registry panel and never in Maria's active lifecycle. Graph, causal timeline, metrics, FHIR, and priority evidence live as staff-only tabs/panels derived from the same projection version; no independent client state may make them disagree.
visual_direction.color: Reuse cool clinical white, ink, indigo, mint, amber, slate, and the landing-only coral/lavender atmosphere. Operational surfaces become predominantly near-opaque white with one-pixel cool borders: indigo means selected/actionable, mint means a verified resolved fact, amber means unresolved/attention, and a muted rose treatment is reserved for provider failure, invalid evidence, or destructive reset warnings. Pending and outcome-unknown use ink/slate structure plus an amber clock or question-mark icon and explicit text, never a reassuring green. Deterministic replay uses a neutral indigo/slate provenance chip while authenticated provider callbacks use a mint-outlined Verified callback chip only after the contract reports provider_callback. Caregiver surfaces remain mint-tinted but not green by default; permission missing/revoked uses a neutral privacy shield and reveals no logistics. FHIR Generated, Validated, Invalid, and Unavailable and ML Available/Unavailable each have icon-and-label treatments, with Validated reserved for validator.passed on the exact current artifact. Coral/lavender remain atmospheric and never encode clinical, transport, model, or validation state.
visual_direction.typography: Retain Outfit for public display and high-level patient moments, Poppins/Plus Jakarta Sans for interface text, and JetBrains Mono only for timestamps, versions, correlation identifiers, artifact hashes, and event references. Public and access copy stays concise and buyer/workspace oriented without demo, prototype, production-auth, Ochsner/Epic connectivity, compliance, autonomous-decision, or guaranteed-outcome claims. Patient language uses short sentence-case headings and plain verbs such as Send my check-in, Review the complete ride plan, and I acknowledge this plan. Staff and transport use compact 11-13px metadata, 14-16px action text, tabular numerals, and explicit Owner / Due / Next action labels. Provider status language follows fact precision: Queued, Sent, Delivered, Answered, Failed, Opted out, Outcome unknown, Reconciliation required, and Recovered are never collapsed into Contacted. ML is always titled Supportive outreach ordering, displays the calibrated probability as staff evidence rather than patient risk, and keeps the fixed statement that it cannot diagnose, determine eligibility, clear treatment, cancel, or reschedule.
visual_direction.spacing_and_shape: Keep the existing 4/8px rhythm and 10/16/24px radii. Public/access cards use 24-32px radii and generous 24-40px padding; patient/caregiver panels use 16-24px radii with at least 16px mobile spacing; staff/transport rows, rails, status tiles, and evidence panels use 10-16px radii and compact 8-16px internal spacing. Use one-pixel structural borders and compact soft shadows, reserving stronger elevation for dialogs and the single current-action card. Maintain 44px targets on public, access, patient, caregiver, and all mobile controls; dense desktop tables keep at least 36px row actions with an equivalent 44px touch presentation on narrow widths. Give skeletons, graph regions, maps, status rails, evidence summaries, and error panels stable minimum dimensions to prevent layout shift. Bound horizontal overflow to labeled lifecycle rails, dense tables, code/artifact viewers, and timeline metadata; document scrolling owns every route and dialogs own at most one vertical scroll region.
visual_direction.component_presentation: Extend the existing Clinical Panel, Status Chip, Metric Tile, Filter Rail, Primary/Secondary button, input, icon well, graph node, and causal timeline vocabulary with six launch patterns. (1) Workspace Entry is a native button with provider mark/text, local destination, and arrow; it performs no credential collection or identity-provider request. (2) Projection Header shows role, last-refreshed time, scenario/projection version, current readiness label, and a refresh action without exposing the scenario token. (3) Owned Work Row always shows type, human owner, due time, status, next action, and closure evidence; explicit transportation/clinical/callback barriers remain above any ML ordering. (4) Provider Truth Strip separates durable intent, provider status, callback provenance, and recovery action; queued is not sent, sent is not delivered, driver assigned is not patient notified, and notification is not acknowledgment. A timeout or uncertain send replaces the initiating button with a Reconciliation required panel and disables blind resend until the server supplies an allowed recovery command. (5) Transport Lifecycle renders notice cutoff, eligibility/funding, service area, accommodations, outbound plan, return plan, offer, acceptance, assignment, notification, acknowledgment, trip progress, failure, backup, escalation, and completion as labeled steps, but emphasizes only states actually present in the contract; closure remains locked until the current plan version is complete and acknowledged. (6) Evidence Panel has a plain-language headline, exact source-event version, inspectable technical details, and an unavailable/invalid treatment that cannot resemble success. The readiness graph uses native buttons for nodes and a companion ordered dependency list; the timeline is an ordered list with actor, event, timestamp, correlation/causation detail, and state change. Reset moves from a header icon to a labeled controlled-action dialog stating that the fixed scenario will be restored and no SMS, call, transport request, callback, or outbox send will be produced; success returns to the configured presentation route only after the server projection reloads. Caregiver renders only caregiver display name, permission state, treatment time/location, provider display name, pickup/return windows, driver/vehicle aliases, transport status, and acknowledgment status; clinical text, staff identity, internal notes, event details, scores, evidence, and hidden search text are not mounted. Transport likewise renders only the contracted fulfillment projection. Existing official logos, route boundaries, fixed target aliases, architecture/security controls, and OpenAPI/event contracts remain authoritative.

motion.strategy: Keep motion subordinate to factual state. Retain the public Continuity Field and the existing one-time landing reveal family, but do not apply arrival animations to operational cards. Route changes use an immediate content swap with focus placement, while confirmed server updates may use a short opacity transition on the exact changed row. Provider-pending states use a static clock/progress label rather than indefinite shimmer after initial loading; lifecycle connectors may make one restrained 300ms progress transition only when a new server projection confirms the next state. Failure, outcome-unknown, invalid evidence, conflict, and revocation appear immediately with no celebratory movement. No animation may imply a provider accepted an action before a verified contract response/callback.
motion.transitions: Use the established 140-200ms hover, focus, press, tab, and panel-state transitions and 180-240ms dialog/panel transitions. Initial skeleton-to-content replacement crossfades for at most 180ms and preserves dimensions. A successful role command highlights the affected row once for 240ms after refreshed server state arrives; idempotent replay receives the same stable end state without a second success flourish. Transport step activation and graph edge resolution use opacity/color transitions under 300ms and never animate layout, scroll position, numbers, clocks, or evidence hashes. Poll/refetch results do not repeatedly animate unchanged content. Patient plan confirmation may retain the existing restrained celebration only after the current plan acknowledgment command succeeds and the refreshed projection reports continuity_plan_confirmed.
motion.microinteractions: Workspace entry, primary actions, filters, tabs, disclosures, and graph nodes use native pressed/focus states with a 1-2px non-touch lift where appropriate. Command buttons become disabled with an in-progress label immediately after activation and stay protected from duplicate submission until the receipt/refetch settles. Validation focuses the error summary then the first invalid field. A stale-version conflict focuses a compact Refresh current state panel, and retry actions identify exactly what will be retried. Timeline rows disclose correlation, causation, version, and provenance without copying secrets. Evidence details use semantic disclosure controls; copy-hash feedback is textual and temporary. The provider strip never spins indefinitely: after the bounded client timeout it changes to Outcome not confirmed and offers Refresh status / Follow recovery guidance, not Send again. Reset requires typing/activating the explicit confirmation control but never exposes the contract confirmation literal as if it were a security secret.
motion.reduced_motion: Effective reduced motion remains the union of live prefers-reduced-motion and the product motion-off setting. Under either signal, all landing reveals render at rest, the Continuity Field is static, smooth scrolling, graph dashes/pulses, skeleton shimmer, lifecycle connector animation, row highlights, dialog movement, hover lifts, dock transforms, confetti, and number transitions are removed. Loading uses static placeholder blocks plus visible text; pending/provider states use icons and labels; route, focus, validation, conflict, recovery, success, and evidence meaning remain identical. Motion preference remains presentation-only and must not be stored with scenario or role data.

responsive.strategy: Design every required route mobile-first from 320px while treating 1024-1440px presentation laptops as the primary staff/transport evidence canvas. Public, pricing, access, patient, and caregiver are single-column through 639px and gain paired modules only when reading order remains obvious. At 768px the access entries may form a two-by-two grid and patient/caregiver summary plus next action may pair. Staff/transport navigation is an in-flow compact grid on narrow widths and a sticky left rail at 1024px; no nested page scroller is introduced. Dense work/evidence tables transform into bordered definition-list cards below 768px. The transport lifecycle is a vertical ordered list on mobile and a labeled horizontal/segmented rail on wide screens; all steps remain in DOM order. Graph nodes stack in dependency order with the companion list; metrics form two columns on mobile and four on wide screens; FHIR report and ML contributors stack before using split panes. Dialogs are bottom-sheet-like on mobile and centered above 640px, with one bounded scroll area and actions that never cover focused fields.
responsive.notes: Verify at 320px, 390x844, 768px, 1024x768, 1440x900, and a wide desktop. Preserve safe-area clearance around the mobile dock, but update navigation so /transport is reachable without hiding another required route; route switching must never reveal a previous role's cached content during load. On narrow staff/transport screens, Owner, Due, Status, and Next action remain above disclosures, evidence hashes wrap safely, and provider/recovery actions remain full-width. Horizontal scrolling is allowed only inside labeled lifecycle, table, code, or filter containers with keyboard access and edge affordances; the page itself must not overflow horizontally. Public imagery, logos, maps, graph regions, skeletons, and async panels retain explicit dimensions. Polling/refetch is bounded and visibility-aware, pauses when the document is hidden, and must not block navigation or duplicate a command.

application_states: Public default: record-free product story, generic continuity capability proof, and no Maria name, MRN, regimen, facility record, readiness graph, timeline, or workspace preview in DOM, accessibility, metadata, or searchable copy.

Public pricing: one configured Small Infusion Center Pilot offer showing $18,000/year and $1,500/month billed annually, separate usage charges, Custom pricing for larger programs, and Request a pilot / Talk to us actions without checkout.
Public enhancement unavailable/reduced motion: all content and navigation remain visible, ordered, and usable without canvas, observer, map, or animation support.

Access default: four native workspace-entry buttons mapping Google to /patient, Microsoft to /caregiver, Apple to /staff, and email to /transport, with no credential fields or external identity-provider network request.
Access route/session invalid or direct deep link without valid local state: no role data flashes; show a brief neutral redirect state and return focus safely to /access.
Role projection loading: route-specific stable skeleton, visible Loading current workspace text, no stale previous-role projection, and navigation remains available.

Role projection empty/not started: calm role-specific opening state with one primary action; staff shows no open work, transport shows no active request, and caregiver shows no authorized plan without placeholder success.

Projection load unavailable or network offline: no optimistic success; distinguish unsent local readiness draft when safe, show last refresh only if data is explicitly marked stale, and offer a bounded retry.

Controlled token missing/invalid (401) or actor/action forbidden (403): remove sensitive content, explain that controlled workspace access is unavailable, and return to /access without presenting the gateway as production authentication.
Rate limited (429): retain form/draft, show Retry-After timing as text, disable automatic repeat, and keep the user on the same route.

Stale aggregate conflict (409): preserve the user's non-sensitive draft, mark it Not submitted, require Refresh current state, and issue any still-valid retry with a new idempotency key rather than overwriting.
Validation/invalid transition (400/422): no state advance; focus a summary, associate field/action errors, and explain the failed guard in plain language.
Command pending: disable the initiating control, label the exact command in progress, leave navigation operable, and never advance a graph/status optimistically.
Command accepted: show accepted/replayed receipt briefly, refetch the authoritative projection, and announce the semantic result once without claiming provider completion.
Readiness baseline: T-3 check-in pending with one primary action and concise treatment time/location; no patient-facing priority score.

Readiness editing: confirmed / needs help / unknown transportation choices, bounded non-urgent clinical words preserved as typed, callback request, validation, unsent-draft, cancel, and submit-disabled states.

Readiness submitted: separate Clinical review, Transportation navigation, and Human callback work cards with owner, due time, status, and next action; explicit barriers remain first regardless of ML ordering.
Patient plan pending: outbound or return plan incomplete, assignment not yet notified, provider failure, or current plan not yet acknowledged keeps continuity visibly at risk/action in progress.

Patient plan ready for acknowledgment: current outbound and return windows, provider, driver/vehicle aliases, plan version, and any human instructions are grouped above one acknowledgment checkbox/action.

Patient plan confirmed: only the refreshed projection's continuity_plan_confirmed state receives mint success and optional motion; stale appointment/provider change immediately reopens the dependency and removes confirmed styling.

Staff owned work: open, assigned, acknowledged, needs information, accepted, actioned, patient informed, patient acknowledged, escalated, and closed states with human owner, SLA/due time, next action, and closure evidence.
Clinical concern: Maria's clearly non-urgent verbatim words remain inert text for staff human review; no model/provider/generic acknowledgment creates clearance or closes undisposed clinical work.

Communication evidence: queued, sent, delivered, undelivered, answered, no answer, failed, opted out, and completed statuses, each labeled SMS/voice, purpose, occurred time when present, and provider_callback versus deterministic_replay provenance.
Communication STOP/opt-out: show SMS unavailable, prohibit follow-up SMS action, keep the barrier open, and present only the allowed voice/manual human path.

Provider outcome unknown: replace success/automatic retry with a persistent Reconciliation required panel, last known intent/attempt, Refresh status, and manual recovery guidance; blind resend remains disabled.

Provider recovery: definitive callback/reconciliation, approved one-time backup, or manual escalation appends to the timeline and updates the affected projection; recovery is never restyled as the original provider having succeeded.
Transport request baseline: notice cutoff, eligibility/funding, service area, mobility/accommodations, notification permission, outbound plan, and return plan shown before offer actions.

Transport lifecycle active: need detected, eligibility reviewed, request ready, offered, accepted, driver assigned, patient notified, patient acknowledged, en route, arrived, picked up, return pending, and completed remain distinct labeled steps.

Transport failure/recovery: declined, cancelled, provider unavailable, stale assignment, return pending, backup required, backup activated, and escalated to navigator each keep the blocker open/reopened with one allowed next action.

Transport provider registry: CareLink Partner Dispatch is active/configured; Uber Health and Lyft Concierge are Disabled / Planned with no action control, credentials indicator, callback state, assignment, or active-trip appearance.
Caregiver permission granted: only authorized transportation logistics and acknowledgment state render, with a visible Logistics only privacy boundary.

Caregiver permission absent/revoked: show a privacy shield and No logistics shared state; remove logistics from visual, accessibility, search, export, cached screen, and outbound content, with no clinical/staff/model/evidence data mounted.
Caregiver loading/error: use only neutral caregiver-shell language; never fall back to a staff or patient projection and never include clinical error detail.

Graph baseline/active/resolved/reopened: treatment event, separate work dependencies, communication/transport proof, and patient acknowledgment render from one projection version with icons, text, connectors, and a mobile ordered-list equivalent.

Causal timeline: chronological event list, role filters, empty filtered result, loading/error, version/correlation/causation disclosure, callback/replay provenance, duplicates/out-of-order callbacks represented without regressing current state.

Metrics evidence: loading, event-derived values with source-event version/as-of, unavailable, no-data/null duration, SLA breach, current blockers, contact attempts, and final-disposition unknown without fabricated zeroes.
FHIR evidence generated: show Generated / validation pending and the exact source-event version; do not display Validated.

FHIR evidence validated: show Validated only when validator.passed is true for the exact current bundle/report, with validator name/version, report summary, and no Epic/Ochsner connectivity or writeback claim.
FHIR invalid/unavailable/hash mismatch: prominent Not validated / Validation unavailable treatment, inspectable report messages, and no mint success or stale Validated badge.

Supportive outreach evidence available: staff-only calibrated percentage, model/schema version, scored time, observed contributor values/directions, source snapshot identity, and fixed supportive-ordering-only boundary.

Supportive outreach score unavailable: artifact missing, malformed, stale, schema mismatch, snapshot mismatch, or runtime error becomes Score unavailable while deterministic cadence and explicit-barrier routing remain operable.
Evidence unauthorized: patient, caregiver, and transport routes do not request, mount, search, cache, or announce staff-only metrics/FHIR/priority content.
Reset confirmation: labeled high-consequence dialog lists what will reset and states that SMS, voice, transport, callbacks, and outbox sends are suppressed.

Reset pending/success/failure: disable duplicate reset, keep external-action suppression language visible, reload authoritative projections before success/route restoration, and never convert interruption into a ready state.

Refresh consistency: after refresh/deep link, every role, graph, timeline, metric, and evidence view reports the same current source/projection version and no browser reducer/local storage competes with server authority.
Responsive and reduced-motion equivalence: every route, failure, recovery, evidence, privacy, focus, and command state remains complete at 320px and presentation widths with all movement removed.
accessibility: Preserve semantic header/nav/main/footer landmarks, add a skip link, maintain one route-level h1, and move focus to the route heading after client navigation or back to /access after an invalid session redirect.

Use native links/buttons/inputs/disclosures and native ordered lists for timelines and lifecycle steps; graph nodes must be buttons rather than div role=button, and every visual connection has an adjacent text dependency description.

Keep the existing high-contrast 2px indigo focus outline plus offset, ensure focused content is never covered by sticky chrome/dock/dialog actions, and maintain logical DOM/tab order independent of wide-screen placement.

Maintain at least WCAG AA contrast, 44px mobile/public/patient/caregiver targets, readable zoom/reflow at 200%, and icon-plus-text treatment for every readiness, provider, transport, privacy, validation, and model state.

Expose loading with aria-busy on the affected region and restrained status text; use role=status for command completion and role=alert only for actionable errors, provider uncertainty, privacy revocation, or invalid evidence. Polling and unchanged refetches must not create repeated announcements.

On validation, conflict, or dependency failure, focus a concise summary linked to the exact field/action; preserve entered non-sensitive text and announce that it was not submitted when authority is uncertain.

Dialogs provide an accessible name/description, initial focus, focus containment, Escape/close behavior where safe, one scroll region, and trigger-focus restoration; reset confirmation does not auto-focus the destructive action.
Status rails, metrics, probability, graphs, and charts provide text/table/list equivalents and never rely on color, position, connector animation, or percentage visualization alone.

Dates/times include full visible context, deadlines and cutoffs are not communicated by countdown alone, null metrics read Not yet available, and identifiers/hashes wrap without truncating their accessible names.

Caregiver and transport privacy is structural: disallowed clinical text, nurse/staff detail, internal notes, model output, evidence, and hidden labels are absent from DOM, accessibility tree, browser find/search index, export, telemetry payloads, and cached role state rather than visually hidden.

Patient free text is rendered as inert text only, never injected HTML; its full preserved value is available to authorized staff without placing it in page titles, live-region announcements, logs, or unrelated error messages.

Provider provenance is included in accessible labels so deterministic replay cannot be mistaken for authenticated live-provider success; outcome unknown and recovery controls state why resend is unavailable.
Honor both OS and product reduced-motion preferences completely while preserving focus movement, content order, progress meaning, all labels, and command results.
assets_or_dependencies: Existing official oncoready-title-logo.svg, compact continuity-loop mark/favicon, and current illustrative public imagery; no new patient or provider photography is required.
Existing React 18, TypeScript strict mode, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Lucide/Tabler icon sets, Leaflet static/live map pattern, and established focus-dialog utility.
Generated OpenAPI boundary types/client from contracts/openapi.yaml; no handwritten endpoints, transport enums, evidence shapes, or provider-success fields.
Existing event JSON schemas for staff timeline labels and evidence relationships; raw callback bodies/secrets are never frontend dependencies.

Existing Continuity Field, ScrollReveal, RideMap static fallback, Treatment Readiness Graph, Audit Timeline, and Clinical Panel/component vocabulary, revised to consume server projections rather than local domain authority.
No new visual or animation runtime dependency; provider entry marks should use simple accessible text/approved local vector treatment and must not introduce an OAuth SDK.
design_system_changes: Add a Provider Truth Strip pattern that visibly separates durable intent, provider state, authenticated callback versus deterministic replay provenance, outcome unknown, and allowed recovery.
Add a Transport Lifecycle pattern with mobile ordered-list and presentation-width rail variants, closure-lock treatment, outbound/return pairing, and failure/backup/escalation branches.

Add an Evidence Panel pattern for source-event version, FHIR validator state/report, metrics nulls, and supportive-outreach explanation/unavailable states without overstating interoperability or clinical authority.
Add a Projection Header and async-state vocabulary covering fresh, refreshing, stale/conflict, degraded, unauthorized, offline, and empty views while preventing prior-role data flash.
Add a privacy-locked caregiver state and codify that role-disallowed content is absent rather than hidden.

Add launch status semantics: mint only for verified resolved facts; amber for unresolved; rose for failure/invalid/destructive warning; neutral ink/amber for uncertainty; provider callback and deterministic replay receive distinct provenance labels.

Preserve the existing public/patient/staff/caregiver/system density, color, typography, radius, focus, motion, and scroll-performance rules; Phase A changes only this report, and the extension may be incorporated into docs/design/DESIGN_SYSTEM.md during Phase B after the digest gate without changing direction.
notes_for_codex: Phase A inspected the current landing, gateway, shared chrome/dock, patient readiness and acknowledgment, staff shell/queue/case, caregiver, graph, timeline, runtime tokens, OpenAPI projection/command/evidence schemas, event schemas, architecture, feature acceptance criteria, and existing design-system evidence. No production frontend code or design-system document was changed.

The former contract blockers are resolved upstream: provider-facing staff/transport projections expose outcome_unknown plus ProviderReconciliationSummary state, attempt provenance, and permitted_recovery; CaregiverProjection uses permission-granted and permission-revoked variants so transport is absent when transport_logistics_allowed is false.
Phase B must begin only after the orchestrator performs a fresh exact digest-bound compatibility review of this amended report, syncs the frontend worktree, and the frontend design gate passes.

The access buttons are local route selectors, not OAuth/social sign-in. They must not collect credentials, load provider SDKs, make identity-provider requests, or imply verified identity; invalid local route/session state returns to /access before role data mounts.

Remove all public patient/workspace proof rather than visually hiding it, and verify absence across DOM, accessibility tree, page metadata, browser find, and built static output. Pricing must come from one configuration and use only Request a pilot / Talk to us actions.

Replace the reducer/localStorage business authority completely for governed launch state. Browser storage may retain only reduced-motion or safe presentation preferences and a clearly unsent non-sensitive draft; role projections must be evicted on route/session change to prevent cross-role flash.

Use only generated OpenAPI types/client and the registered event schemas. If implementation needs any status, action, endpoint, field, or conditional response not present after orchestrator reconciliation, stop with CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUIRED rather than creating a UI-only domain state.

Provider UI is evidence-first: accepted/queued is not delivered, assignment is not notification, notification is not acknowledgment, deterministic replay is not a live callback, and a network timeout is not permission to retry a consequential action.

Caregiver and transport components should accept their exact minimized projection types rather than a broad staff/scenario object. Add negative source/DOM/accessibility/search/cache tests for clinical words, nurse/staff details, internal notes, priority output, and evidence.

Planned Uber Health and Lyft Concierge entries are static disabled registry metadata outside Maria's active workflow. No logo treatment may make them appear configured, and they receive no button, credential, callback, assignment, trip, or success state.

Evidence and ML design should be implemented last within the frontend slice after route/projection/provider recovery work is stable. FHIR Validated requires the exact passing validator state; Score unavailable is a first-class safe state and never weakens deterministic routing.

Phase B verification should include generated-client freshness, build/typecheck/lint, focused component tests for every async/conflict/privacy/provider/evidence state, route/deep-link and no-provider-request tests, caregiver negative-disclosure tests, reduced-motion checks, keyboard/focus/dialog checks, responsive Playwright at 320/390/768/1024/1440 widths, refresh consistency, safe reset with no external effects, and the complete failure-and-recovery journey.
Ready for orchestrator compatibility review and canonical SHA-256 binding. Any post-approval edit to this report requires a fresh review before production frontend changes.
